problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{-9x+36}{(x-3)(x-6)}=-\frac{3}{(x-3)}+\frac{B}{(x-6)},
$$

what is the value of $B?$
worked_solution:
Our task is to find $B$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-9x+36}{(x-3)(x-6)}=-\frac{3}{(x-3)}+\frac{B}{(x-6)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $(x-3)(x-6)$ gives

$$
-9x+36=-3(x-6)+B(x-3).
$$

For $x=6$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-9(6)+36 & =-3(6-6)+B(6-3) \\ -18 & =3B \\ B & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
